sections.content: To say how you feel, use *vagyok* with an adjective: *Éhes vagyok.* (I am hungry.) *Szomjas vagyok.* (I am thirsty.) For a person other than *én* or *te*, *van* is left out as you know: *Anna éhes.* The same works for food: *A leves finom.* (The soup is delicious.)

sections.title: How you feel and how it tastes
Feeling and doing
sections.content: A waiter is a *pincér*. You can say how you feel first and then what you do: *Éhes vagyok. Eszem egy szendvicset.* Put *nagyon* (very) before the adjective, as you know: *nagyon finom*.

items.spanish: Szomjas vagyok. Iszom egy pohár vizet.
items.english: I am thirsty. I drink a glass of water.

sections.content: *Nem vagyok éhes* is “I am not hungry”. *Nincs* is for things that are not there, not for how you feel.
